environment.deployment: Docker Desktop; API, MySQL 8, Redis 7 and Kafka on one host; unrelated Dify containers stopped during timed rounds

scope: authenticated end-to-end seckill admission; 3000 distinct JWT users per round; login and one Producer warm-up request excluded from timed phase

design.baseline: sync Kafka ACK + per-request activity DB read
design.optimized: recoverable async Reservation + 2-second Caffeine activity metadata cache
design.common: same image, 4-vCPU/1.5-GiB API limit, 128 Tomcat threads, 20 Hikari connections, 3 Kafka consumer threads, Redis Lua inventory

ablation.description: with activity cache enabled in both variants, changing only sync ACK to async Reservation did not help on the same-host Kafka setup
ablation.interpretation: local broker ACK was cheap; faster admission increased instantaneous MySQL consumer contention, so the cache was the material part of the combined gain

coldStartRecovery.observation: before topics and Producer metadata were warmed, 110 Kafka send errors were logged in the first async round because max.block.ms was 50 ms
coldStartRecovery.result: all 3000 accepted reservations converged to 3000 database orders; stock reached zero and reservation pending returned to zero
coldStartRecovery.lesson: pre-create topics and warm Producer metadata before steady-state capacity tests; keep the cold-start run as recovery evidence, not as capacity evidence

limitations: Each timed round was a short 3000-request burst lasting about 2-3 seconds, not a 3-5 minute soak test or production SLO.
Load generator and services shared one physical host; the result is a local engineering A/B, not a cloud or distributed production benchmark.
The optimized P95 median increased by 6.64% and the third optimized round had a high P99 outlier; do not claim that every latency percentile improved.
Use the three-round median and preserve every raw round; do not present the 1573.20-QPS or 1489.61-QPS single round as a stable capacity ceiling.
